intro: You go to the barber, the laundry or the bengkel, and someone else does the job. In English that's 'I had my hair cut' or 'I need to get my glasses fixed'. Today you'll learn have/get + thing + third form for services, why word order changes the meaning, and how the same pattern tells bad news like 'I had my phone stolen'.
teachingNotes: Recap in one line (b1-passive-intro and b2-passive-voice): passive = be + third form (past participle), My car was repaired. New form: have + object (the thing) + third form = someone else does the work, usually because you arranged or paid for it: I had my hair cut. I have my car serviced every six months. The third form is the same one as in the passive and never changes. have works in every tense and is a normal verb, so questions and negatives use do/does/did: Where do you have your hair cut? I didn't have it cleaned. Tenses to practise: have/has (habit), had (past), have/has had (present perfect: We've had the house cleaned), am/is/are having (arranged future: We're having our bathroom renovated next month), will have (I'll have it delivered), need to / should / going to + have/get … done.

Indonesian trap (common error 1): Indonesian uses an active verb for services that someone else does: saya potong rambut, saya cuci motor, saya servis AC, saya fotokopi KTP. In English 'I cut my hair at the barber's' / 'I washed my motorbike' mean you did it yourself, so learners must say I had my hair cut / I had my motorbike washed. Native speakers do sometimes say 'I cut my hair' loosely, but teach and test the clear contrast with context (paid someone vs did it myself). Explain cut → cut → cut (third form = base form, also put, set) so 'had my hair cut' doesn't look like a broken rule; 'cutted' doesn't exist.

get + object + third form (common error 2): same meaning for services, more informal and very common in speech, especially after need to / have to / should / going to: I need to get my glasses fixed; You should get that checked. Learners drop the third form: *'I got my laptop fix' → fixed (Indonesian dibetulkan has di-, English needs the third form). Also wrong: *'get it fixing'. Both British and American English use have and get here; get is more casual. Don't make have vs get an either-or question: when both fit, accept both, and only test the form and word order. Don't teach have someone do / get someone to do (I had the mechanic check it, I got Budi to help); if asked, say it's a related pattern for later.

Word order (common error 3): the thing goes BETWEEN have and the third form. I had my car repaired (a mechanic did it) ≠ I had repaired my car (past perfect: I did it myself, before another past moment, which they know from B1). Similarly I've had my car repaired (someone else) ≠ I've repaired my car (me). Check: is the thing before or after the third form?

Bad experiences (objective talk-about-services): the same pattern says something bad was done to you that nobody arranged: I had my phone stolen on the KRL, Bu Ani had her account hacked, I had my flight cancelled (British cancelled, American canceled). Compare the passive My phone was stolen (focus on the phone) with I had my phone stolen (focus on me). Errors: *'I had stolen my phone' (says I was the thief), *'had my phone stole'. 'I got my phone stolen' is heard in casual talk, but teach and test had.

Everyday services in Indonesian contexts: potong rambut (have/get my hair cut, at the barber's / hairdresser's: British; American at the barber / barbershop), cuci motor or mobil (get the car washed), servis motor / AC (have the motorbike / air conditioner serviced; Indonesians say AC 'a-se', English says air conditioner, British air con, American AC 'ay-see'), laundry kiloan (have your shirts washed and ironed), fotokopi (get your KTP photocopied; KTP = ID card), jilid skripsi (have your thesis printed and bound), delivery (have it delivered). Scope: no third conditional, wish, past modals or participle clauses.

keyPoints.title: have + thing + third form: someone else does it
keyPoints.explanation: Use have + the thing + the third form when someone else does a job for you, usually because you arranged or paid for it: I had my hair cut (the barber cut it). Indonesian says 'saya potong rambut' even when the barber does it, but English 'I cut my hair' means you held the scissors yourself. The thing goes between have and the third form: I had my car repaired (a mechanic did it) is not I had repaired my car (past perfect: you did it). have works in every tense: I have it serviced every year, I've had it serviced, I'm having it serviced tomorrow, I'll have it delivered. cut stays cut: cut → cut → cut.

id.title: have + benda + bentuk ketiga: orang lain yang mengerjakan
id.explanation: Pakai have + bendanya + bentuk ketiga kalau orang lain yang mengerjakan sesuatu untukmu, biasanya karena kamu yang mengatur atau membayarnya: I had my hair cut (tukang cukur yang memotong). Bahasa Indonesia bilang 'saya potong rambut' walaupun tukang cukurnya yang memotong, tapi 'I cut my hair' dalam bahasa Inggris berarti kamu sendiri yang memegang guntingnya. Bendanya ada di ANTARA have dan bentuk ketiga: I had my car repaired (montir yang memperbaiki) berbeda dengan I had repaired my car (past perfect: kamu sendiri yang memperbaiki). have bisa dipakai di semua tense: I have it serviced every year, I've had it serviced, I'm having it serviced tomorrow, I'll have it delivered. cut tetap cut: cut → cut → cut.

keyPoints.title: get + thing + third form: the casual version
keyPoints.explanation: In everyday speech, get + thing + third form means the same as have for services, but sounds more casual. It's very common after need to, have to, should and going to: I need to get my glasses fixed. You should get that checked. The last word is still the third form: 'I got my laptop fix' is wrong → I got my laptop fixed. British and American English both use it.

Pola ini sangat sering muncul setelah need to, have to, should dan going to: I need to get my glasses fixed. You should get that checked. Kata terakhirnya tetap bentuk ketiga: 'I got my laptop fix' salah → I got my laptop fixed. Bahasa Inggris British dan Amerika sama-sama memakainya.

keyPoints.title: Services and bad experiences
keyPoints.explanation: Use the pattern for everyday services (a haircut, laundry, a repair, photocopies, a delivery) and also for bad things that were done to you, when nobody arranged anything: I had my phone stolen on the KRL. Compare the passive My phone was stolen (the story is about the phone) with I had my phone stolen (the story is about you). Don't say 'I had stolen my phone': that means you were the thief.

blocks.text:
Quick recap from the passive: **be + the third form** (the past participle, V3) puts the thing first: *My car **was repaired**.* It doesn't say who arranged it.

Today's pattern adds **you**: **have + the thing + the third form**. It means **someone else** did the job, usually because you arranged or paid for it:
- *I **had my car repaired**.* (a mechanic repaired it; I paid)
- *Bu Ani **has her car serviced** every six months.* (the bengkel does it)

**The Indonesian trap:** Indonesian uses a normal active verb even when someone else does the work: *saya potong rambut*, *saya cuci motor*, *saya servis AC*. Translated word by word, *I cut my hair* or *I washed my motorbike* tells an English speaker that **you** held the scissors or the hose. If you paid someone, say ***I had my hair cut***.

id.text:
Ringkasan dari pelajaran passive: **be + bentuk ketiga** (past participle, V3) menaruh bendanya di depan: *My car **was repaired**.* Kalimat ini tidak bilang siapa yang mengaturnya.

Pola hari ini menambahkan **kamu**: **have + bendanya + bentuk ketiga**. Artinya **orang lain** yang mengerjakan, biasanya karena kamu yang mengatur atau membayarnya:
- *I **had my car repaired**.* (montir yang memperbaiki; saya yang bayar)
- *Bu Ani **has her car serviced** every six months.* (bengkel yang mengerjakan)

**Jebakan bahasa Indonesia:** bahasa Indonesia memakai kata kerja aktif biasa walaupun orang lain yang mengerjakan: *saya potong rambut*, *saya cuci motor*, *saya servis AC*. Kalau diterjemahkan kata per kata, *I cut my hair* atau *I washed my motorbike* membuat penutur bahasa Inggris mengira **kamu sendiri** yang memegang gunting atau selangnya. Kalau kamu membayar orang lain, bilang ***I had my hair cut***.

blocks.text: Why *had my hair **cut***, not 'cutted'? Because **cut → cut → cut**: its third form looks exactly like the base verb. A few verbs work like this, for example *put* and *set*. So in *I had my hair cut*, **cut** is the third form, just like *repaired* in *I had my car repaired*.

id.text: Kenapa *had my hair **cut***, bukan 'cutted'? Karena **cut → cut → cut**: bentuk ketiganya sama persis dengan bentuk dasarnya. Ada beberapa kata kerja seperti ini, misalnya *put* dan *set*. Jadi di *I had my hair cut*, **cut** adalah bentuk ketiga, sama seperti *repaired* di *I had my car repaired*.

blocks.text:
The same words in a different order mean something completely different. Look at **where the thing is**:
- *I **had my car repaired** last week.* → the thing (*my car*) is **between** had and the third form: **a mechanic** did it.
- *I **had repaired** my car before the trip.* → **had + third form** together is the **past perfect** (from B1): **you** did it, before another moment in the past.

The same with the present perfect: *I've **had my car repaired*** (someone else) vs *I've **repaired** my car* (me).

**have works in every tense.** Change *have* and keep the rest:
- habit: *I **have** my car serviced every year.*
- past: *I **had** it serviced last month.*
- present perfect: *I've **had** it serviced.*
- arranged future: *I'm **having** it serviced tomorrow.*
- will / need to / going to: *I'll **have** it delivered. I need to **have** it checked.*

id.text:
Kata-kata yang sama dengan urutan berbeda punya arti yang sama sekali lain. Perhatikan **di mana bendanya**:
- *I **had my car repaired** last week.* → bendanya (*my car*) ada **di antara** had dan bentuk ketiga: **montir** yang mengerjakan.
- *I **had repaired** my car before the trip.* → **had + bentuk ketiga** yang berdampingan adalah **past perfect** (dari B1): **kamu sendiri** yang mengerjakan, sebelum suatu waktu lain di masa lalu.

Sama juga dengan present perfect: *I've **had my car repaired*** (orang lain) vs *I've **repaired** my car* (saya sendiri).

**have bisa dipakai di semua tense.** Ubah *have*-nya saja, sisanya tetap:
- kebiasaan: *I **have** my car serviced every year.*
- lampau: *I **had** it serviced last month.*
- present perfect: *I've **had** it serviced.*
- rencana yang sudah diatur: *I'm **having** it serviced tomorrow.*
- will / need to / going to: *I'll **have** it delivered. I need to **have** it checked.*

material.title: get something done: the casual version

blocks.text:
In everyday speech, people often use **get** instead of have: **get + the thing + the third form**. For services the meaning is the same; *get* just sounds more casual and is very common after **need to, have to, should, going to**:
- *I need to **get my glasses fixed** this week.*
- *Where did you **get your hair cut**? It looks great.*
- *You should **get that cough checked**.*

British and American English both use it. In a formal email, *have* sounds a little more careful.

The most common mistake: forgetting the third form. *Laptopnya dibetulkan* has **di-**, and di- means the thing receives the action, so English needs the third form: 'I got my laptop **fix**' ✗ → *I got my laptop **fixed*** ✓.

id.text:
Dalam percakapan sehari-hari, orang sering memakai **get** sebagai ganti have: **get + bendanya + bentuk ketiga**. Untuk layanan, artinya sama; *get* hanya terdengar lebih santai dan sangat sering muncul setelah **need to, have to, should, going to**:
- *I need to **get my glasses fixed** this week.*
- *Where did you **get your hair cut**? It looks great.*
- *You should **get that cough checked**.*

Bahasa Inggris British dan Amerika sama-sama memakainya. Di email formal, *have* terdengar sedikit lebih rapi.

Kesalahan paling umum: lupa bentuk ketiga. *Laptopnya dibetulkan* punya **di-**, dan di- berarti bendanya yang dikenai tindakan, jadi bahasa Inggris butuh bentuk ketiga: 'I got my laptop **fix**' ✗ → *I got my laptop **fixed*** ✓.

blocks.text: Don't mix this up with *My phone **got stolen*** from the passive lesson. There, *get* works like *be* and there's **no thing in the middle**. In *I **got my laptop fixed***, the thing (*my laptop*) sits between get and the third form, and **you** are the one who arranged it.

id.text: Jangan tertukar dengan *My phone **got stolen*** dari pelajaran passive. Di sana, *get* bekerja seperti *be* dan **tidak ada benda di tengahnya**. Di *I **got my laptop fixed***, bendanya (*my laptop*) ada di antara get dan bentuk ketiga, dan **kamu** yang mengaturnya.

blocks.prompt: The zip on my backpack is broken. I'll get it ___ at the market.
blocks.explain: get + thing + **third form**: *get it replaced* (someone at the market replaces it). 'get it replace' has no third form, and 'get it replacing' would mean the zip does the replacing.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: The zip on my backpack is broken. I'll get it ___ at the market.
id.explain: get + benda + **bentuk ketiga**: *get it replaced* (orang di pasar yang menggantinya). 'get it replace' tidak punya bentuk ketiga, dan 'get it replacing' berarti ritsletingnya yang mengganti sesuatu.

blocks.text: Here are services you use all the time, said the English way. In each one, someone else does the work, so English uses **have/get + the thing + the third form**, while Indonesian just uses the verb.

id.text: Ini layanan yang sering kamu pakai, dalam bahasa Inggris. Di setiap contoh, orang lain yang mengerjakan, jadi bahasa Inggris memakai **have/get + bendanya + bentuk ketiga**, sedangkan bahasa Indonesia cukup memakai kata kerjanya.

material.title: When something bad happens to you

blocks.text:
The same pattern also tells **bad news**: something was done to you or your things, and **nobody arranged it**.
- *I **had my phone stolen** on the KRL.* (HP-ku dicopet di KRL)
- *Bu Ani **had her email account hacked**.* (akunnya diretas)
- *We **had our flight cancelled** because of the storm.* (British *cancelled*, American *canceled*)

You didn't pay a thief! Here *have* just means *this happened to me*. Compare it with the passive you already know:
- *My phone **was stolen**.* → the story is about the phone.
- *I **had my phone stolen**.* → the story is about **you**.
Both are correct. In casual talk you may hear 'I got my phone stolen', but **had** is the safe choice.

Watch the order again: 'I **had stolen** my phone' is the past perfect and says **you** were the thief.

id.text:
Pola yang sama juga dipakai untuk **kabar buruk**: sesuatu menimpamu atau barangmu, dan **tidak ada yang mengaturnya**.
- *I **had my phone stolen** on the KRL.* (HP-ku dicopet di KRL)
- *Bu Ani **had her email account hacked**.* (akunnya diretas)
- *We **had our flight cancelled** because of the storm.* (British *cancelled*, Amerika *canceled*)

Kamu kan tidak membayar pencuri! Di sini *have* hanya berarti *ini terjadi pada saya*. Bandingkan dengan passive yang sudah kamu kenal:
- *My phone **was stolen**.* → ceritanya tentang HP-nya.
- *I **had my phone stolen**.* → ceritanya tentang **kamu**.
Dua-duanya benar. Dalam obrolan santai kamu mungkin dengar 'I got my phone stolen', tapi **had** adalah pilihan yang aman.

Perhatikan urutannya lagi: 'I **had stolen** my phone' adalah past perfect dan berarti **kamu sendiri** pencurinya.

blocks.prompt: Bu Ani's flight to Medan was cancelled because of bad weather. Complete: Bu Ani ___ .
blocks.explain: The airline cancelled it and it happened to her: *had her flight cancelled* (had + thing + third form). 'cancelled her flight' and 'had cancelled her flight' (past perfect) both say Bu Ani cancelled it herself.

id.prompt: Penerbangan Bu Ani ke Medan dibatalkan karena cuaca buruk. Lengkapi: Bu Ani ___ .
id.explain: Maskapainya yang membatalkan dan itu menimpa Bu Ani: *had her flight cancelled* (had + benda + bentuk ketiga). 'cancelled her flight' dan 'had cancelled her flight' (past perfect) sama-sama berarti Bu Ani sendiri yang membatalkannya.

suggestedQuestions: What's the difference between 'I cut my hair' and 'I had my hair cut'?
Can I always use get instead of have?
Why is 'I had my phone stolen' correct if I didn't ask anyone to steal it?
How is 'I had my car repaired' different from 'My car was repaired'?

id.intro: Kamu pergi ke tukang cukur, laundry atau bengkel, dan orang lain yang mengerjakan. Dalam bahasa Inggris itu jadi 'I had my hair cut' atau 'I need to get my glasses fixed'. Hari ini kamu belajar have/get + benda + bentuk ketiga untuk layanan, kenapa urutan kata mengubah arti, dan bagaimana pola yang sama dipakai untuk kabar buruk seperti 'I had my phone stolen'.
suggestedQuestions: Apa bedanya 'I cut my hair' dan 'I had my hair cut'?
Apakah get selalu bisa dipakai sebagai ganti have?
Kenapa 'I had my phone stolen' benar, padahal aku tidak menyuruh siapa pun mencurinya?
Apa bedanya 'I had my car repaired' dan 'My car was repaired'?

assessment.caus-1: Tulis ulang kalimatnya dalam bahasa Inggris, diawali dengan 'I had' (kamu yang membayar; fotografernya yang bekerja): A photographer at the studio took my passport photo yesterday.
assessment.caus-2: Pak Hasan tidak memperbaiki atapnya sendiri: dia membayar tukang untuk mengerjakannya bulan lalu. Perbaiki kalimatnya: Pak Hasan had repaired his roof last month.
assessment.caus-3: Perbaiki kesalahannya: I'm going to get my phone screen repair this afternoon.
assessment.caus-4: Lengkapi dengan get + 'my eyes' + bentuk yang tepat dari 'test': I can't read the slides in meetings any more. I need to ___ soon.
assessment.caus-5: Tulis ulang dalam bahasa Inggris sebagai pengalaman buruk, diawali dengan 'Budi had': Someone stole Budi's sandals while he was praying at the mosque.
assessment.caus-6: Temanmu bertanya: 'Do you wash your clothes yourself?' Lengkapi jawabanmu dengan have atau get + 'my clothes' + bentuk yang tepat dari 'wash' (ini kebiasaan, jadi present simple): No, I ___ at the laundry kiloan near my kos every week.
assessment.caus-7: Lengkapi dengan present continuous dari have + 'our kitchen' + bentuk yang tepat dari 'paint' (tukang catnya sudah dipesan untuk minggu depan): We can't cook at home next week because we ___ .
